content:
`¬(P ↔ Q)` means that `P` ,`Q` don't have the same truth value, i.e. one of them is true and the other is false.

$
\\begin{array}{|c | c|c|}
\\hline
P & Q & \\text{¬(P ↔ Q)} \\\\\\\\
\\hline
T & T & F \\\\\\\\
\\hline
F & F & F \\\\\\\\
\\hline
T & F & T \\\\\\\\
\\hline
F & T & T \\\\\\\\
\\hline
\\end{array}
$

We can conclude that for `¬(P ↔ Q)`:
- `¬P`,`Q` have the same truth value (`¬P ↔ Q`)
- `P`,`¬Q` have the same truth value (`P ↔ ¬Q`).
